harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1's GRUB config so the kernel boots with audit=1 persistently, verified via grub.cfg regeneration and a live reboot that the parameter is present and the kernel audit subsystem initializes.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Ubuntu 24.04, GRUB2 bootloader, found /etc/default/grub.d/50-cloudimg-settings.cfg overrides GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT
Backed up /etc/default/grub, set GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="audit=1" (not overridden by the cloudimg drop-in, applied to all boot entries including recovery)
Ran update-grub and verified /boot/grub/grub.cfg contains audit=1 in all three linux boot entries (normal, advanced, recovery)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and uptime baseline, confirmed GRUB_DEFAULT=0 with no saved_entry override so the normal entry (with audit=1) is default
Issued sudo systemctl reboot in background so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed (901ef286... -> a7ba7953...) proving an actual restart occurred
Verified post-reboot /proc/cmdline contains audit=1 and dmesg shows 'audit: enabled (after initialization)' confirming functional persistence

evidence.requirement: Kernel configured to boot with audit=1 (config change)
evidence.summary: Identified GRUB setup and cloudimg override risk, set GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="audit=1" in /etc/default/grub, ran update-grub, and confirmed audit=1 present in all grub.cfg linux boot entries
Captured pre-restart boot_id (901ef286-c79c-44c0-ad2c-cfde1f6daa7a), uptime, and confirmed GRUB_DEFAULT=0 with no saved_entry override
Issued 'sudo systemctl reboot' backgrounded; stream closed as node went down, confirming the reboot command was accepted and executed

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving actual restart (node1)
evidence.summary: Polled node1 until reachable; new boot_id a7ba7953-a442-46bc-ab9f-2f16892504f6 differs from pre-restart 901ef286-c79c-44c0-ad2c-cfde1f6daa7a, and uptime shows a fresh boot time

evidence.requirement: audit=1 persisted across the real reboot and audit subsystem functional (node1)
evidence.summary: Post-reboot /proc/cmdline contains audit=1; dmesg shows kernel command line with audit=1 and 'audit: enabled (after initialization)' plus active audit log entries, proving the setting took effect on the actual boot, not just the config file

attempts.summary: Configured node1's GRUB config so the kernel boots with audit=1 persistently, verified via grub.cfg regeneration and a live reboot that the parameter is present and the kernel audit subsystem initializes.
